title: Safe Error Messages and Information Disclosure
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of safe error messages and information disclosure.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Errors should help users recover and help maintainers diagnose problems without revealing secrets, internal paths, database details, stack traces, tokens, or private data. User-facing messages should be understandable and non-sensitive; detailed diagnostics belong in protected logs with appropriate access and redaction. Avoid swallowing errors silently.
understand.whyItMatters: Error handling is part of the security boundary because failures can expose internal information or leave users confused.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Errors should help users recover and help maintainers diagnose problems without revealing secrets, internal paths, database details, stack traces, tokens, or private data. User-facing messages should be understandable and non-sensitive; detailed diagnostics belong in protected logs with appropriate access and redaction. Avoid swallowing errors silently.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.title: Show a safe message
examples.code:
const message = 'Unable to save. Please try again.';
console.log(message);
examples.expectedOutput: Unable to save. Please try again.
examples.explanation: A generic message gives a recovery path without revealing internals.

examples.title: Log a category, not a secret
examples.explanation: A code helps support without logging credentials.

examples.title: Separate details from user view
examples.explanation: Technical details can be stored in restricted diagnostics.

examples.title: Redact sensitive values
examples.explanation: Redaction is illustrative; logs need careful review and controls.

examples.title: Avoid silent failure
examples.code:
const handled = true;
console.log(handled ? 'record error and guide recovery' : 'ignore error');
examples.explanation: Handled errors should be observable and actionable.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Design an error response for a failed login, failed file upload, and server timeout. For each, write a user-safe message and decide what diagnostic detail can be logged without sensitive values.
steps: Design an error response for a failed login, failed file upload, and server timeout. For each, write a user-safe message and decide what diagnostic detail can be logged without sensitive values.
Identify the relevant assets, inputs, or permissions.
Choose a control and explain why it applies.
Check edge cases and failure behavior.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Create an error-handling policy for a beginner app: user messages, log levels, redaction, access to logs, retention, and recovery guidance.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Create an error-handling policy for a beginner app: user messages, log levels, redaction, access to logs, retention, and recovery guidance.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.

hints: Do not expose stack traces to ordinary users.
Never log passwords, tokens, or unnecessary personal details.
Use consistent error codes where helpful.
